title: Flat trait pinching and arbitrary scalar extension
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $X,Z,T$ be flat $S$-schemes [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $j:Z\to T$ a finite $S$-morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Suppose an affine open $U\subseteq X$ contains $i(Z)$. Let $P=X\amalg_ZT$ be a pushout in the category of all schemes [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with maps $a:X\to P$, $b:T\to P$, and $c=ai=bj$. Then $P\to S$ is flat. For every commutative $R$-algebra $R'$, with $S'=\operatorname{Spec}R'$, the base-changed square $Z_{S'}\to X_{S'}$, $Z_{S'}\to T_{S'}$, $X_{S'}\to P_{S'}$, $T_{S'}\to P_{S'}$ is again a pushout of schemes [def-pc-base-change]. This assertion includes nonflat $R'$ and zero rings. More explicitly, $P$ has a simultaneous affine cover with coordinate rings $Q=A\times_D E$, where the rings of the inverse images in $X,Z,T$ are respectively $A,D,E$, $A\to D$ is surjective, and the fibre product has coordinatewise operations. The sequence of $R$-modules $$0\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow A\oplus E\xrightarrow{(u,v)\mapsto\bar u-j^*v}D\longrightarrow0$$ is short exact, $Q$ is $R$-flat, and the canonical algebra map $$Q\otimes_RR'\longrightarrow (A\otimes_RR')\times_{D\otimes_RR'}(E\otimes_RR')$$ is an isomorphism for every $R'$. These identifications give the base-changed pushout square on each chart and agree on all open restrictions. No properness, finite-type, etaleness, surjectivity of $j$, or fibre-dimension assumption is imposed.

proof.text: The finite morphism $j$ is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-iff-integral-lft]. The given affine open containing all of $i(Z)$ contains every $i(j^{-1}(t))$, including empty fibres. Thus [lem-sfb-ferrand-scheme-pushout] applies. Its pushout is uniquely isomorphic, respecting $X,T,Z$, to the given $P$ by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; the same uniqueness identifies the induced map to $S$. Use its simultaneous affine cover $W=\operatorname{Spec}Q$ with inverse-image rings $A,E,D$, $A\twoheadrightarrow D$, and $Q=A\times_DE$. This already supplies the coordinatewise ring structure asserted in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0E25, proposition-pushout-along-closed-immersion-and-integral, affine-cover paragraph; morphisms.tex Tag 01WJ, lemma-finite-integral

proof.text: Fix a chart and write $\alpha:A\twoheadrightarrow D$ and $\beta:E\to D$. The inclusion $Q\to A\oplus E$ is injective, its image is exactly the kernel of the $R$-linear difference map $\delta(u,v)=\alpha(u)-\beta(v)$, and $\delta$ is surjective: lift any $d\in D$ to $u\in A$ and use $(u,0)$. This proves the displayed short exact sequence directly; the difference map is used as a module map, not as a ring homomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0E25, affine fibre-product description; direct kernel calculation

proof.text: The affine criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] applied to the inverse-image opens in the flat $S$-schemes $X,T,Z$ gives $R$-flatness of $A,E,D$. For $0\ne r\in R$, multiplication by $r$ on $R$ is injective since $R$ is a domain [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Tensoring this injection with $A$ or $E$ is injective by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; under $R\otimes_RA=A$ and $R\otimes_RE=E$ it is multiplication by $r$. Therefore $r(u,v)=0$ in the submodule $Q\subseteq A\oplus E$ forces $u=v=0$. The DVR is a PID by the cited definition, so [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] makes $Q$ flat. Now [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] makes each $W\to S$ flat. These opens cover $P$, and the local rings of an open subscheme at its points are the same local rings as in $P$; hence $P\to S$ is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0AUW, lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat (1); morphisms.tex Tag 01U5, lemma-flat-characterize; algebra.tex Tag 00HB, definition-flat

proof.text: Let $R'$ be any commutative $R$-algebra. Since the last term $D$ of step 2 is $R$-flat, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] applies with $N=R'$ and preserves the entire short exact sequence. Interchanging tensor factors gives $0\to Q\otimes_RR'\to (A\oplus E)\otimes_RR'\to D\otimes_RR'\to0$. No flatness of $R'$ is used: it is flatness of the quotient $D$ that supplies the initial zero.

The module isomorphism $(A\oplus E)\otimes_RR'\simeq(A\otimes_RR')\oplus(E\otimes_RR')$ sends $(u,v)\otimes r'$ to $(u\otimes r',v\otimes r')$; its inverse is the sum of the maps from the two summand inclusions. They are inverse on pure tensors and hence on sums. Under it the last map in step 4 is $\alpha\otimes1-\beta\otimes1$. Its kernel is precisely the underlying module of $(A\otimes_RR')\times_{D\otimes_RR'}(E\otimes_RR')$. Exactness therefore makes the canonical map from $Q\otimes_RR'$ to that fibre product bijective. Its formula $(u,v)\otimes r'\mapsto(u\otimes r',v\otimes r')$ preserves the unit and products of pure tensors, and then all products by distributivity. It is consequently the asserted algebra isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00HL, lemma-flat-tor-zero, applied to the difference-map sequence; elementary identification of its kernel

proof.text: Base change of the affine chart and its inverse images has rings $Q\otimes_RR'$, $A\otimes_RR'$, $E\otimes_RR'$, $D\otimes_RR'$ with the canonical tensor maps, by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. The map $\alpha\otimes1$ is surjective: lift each first factor of each pure tensor in a finite sum. Step 5 and [lem-sfb-affine-closed-pinching-pushout] thus give a pushout in the category of all schemes over every $W_{S'}$. These are open subschemes of $P_{S'}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and cover it, since every point projects into some $W$.

source.place: Tag 0ET0, lemma-basic-example-pushout; schemes.tex Tags 01I4/01JQ, affine fibre products

proof.text: For $h=(u,v)\in Q$, [lem-sfb-ring-fibre-product-spectrum] identifies the inverse-image rings over the principal open $D(h)\subseteq W$ with $A_u,E_v,D_{\alpha(u)}$ and identifies $Q_h$ with their fibre product. The comparison of step 5 restricts to the same comparison there: both composites with its two projections are the tensor maps of the coordinate projections. Thus the maps agree by the defining equality of pairs in a fibre product. Repeating steps 3--6 on this affine open is valid because the three source opens still belong to the original flat schemes. Principal opens contained in $W\cap V$ cover each chart intersection by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open]; their pullbacks cover the corresponding intersection after scalar extension. Given compatible maps $X_{S'}\to H$ and $T_{S'}\to H$ to any scheme $H$, step 6 gives a unique map $W_{S'}\to H$ on each chart. On these principal-open refinements the maps from different charts agree by the local pushout uniqueness. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] they agree on the intersections and glue uniquely to $P_{S'}\to H$. This is the global pushout universal property. The same restriction argument gives agreement on every open, without assuming chart intersections affine. If $R'=0$, all base-changed rings and schemes are zero and empty respectively, and every calculation and universal property above still holds.
